# composer_driver_parity fixtures

## 2026-07-02 — `induce_concern.json`'s `covered` case updated (v1.2.0 literal decode)

Creator directive: "transformation is quantum change in a specific dimension" (see
`TRANSFORM_DESIGN.md` and `seeds/shape_decode_loop.json`'s v1.2.0 comment). `sd_decode`'s
three `ShapeDecode` invocations flipped from `wild_objects=true` to LITERAL, making the new
`sd_transform_decode`/`sd_recognize_transformed` stage load-bearing instead of decorative.

**What changed in this file:** ONLY `covered.result` (and, mechanically, nothing else —
`covered.observation`, `uncovered`, and `parts` are confirmed byte-identical to the prior
capture; verified programmatically, not by eye, before overwriting).

**Before** (`wild_objects=true`; the object slots were wildcarded away before scoring, so an
observation sharing a held part's predicate skeleton was fully covered regardless of its
argument values):

```json
"result": {
  "covered_by": "part_move",
  "minted": false,
  "note": "held term-shape 'part_move' covers the observation — no new concern (the null)",
  "observation": [["move", "Y", "by", "Z"], ["stop", "Y"]]
}
```

**After** (literal decode leaves a real residual for the `X->Y`/`D->Z` filler rename;
`sd_transform_decode` explains it as identity + a per-dimension quantum delta on
`part_move`, so `sd_recognize_transformed` fires instead of `sd_recognize`):

```json
"result": {
  "covered_by": "part_move",
  "minted": false,
  "note": "held term-shape 'part_move' covers the observation UNDER A TRANSFORM (identity + a
           per-dimension quantum delta) — no new concern, recognition-under-transformation
           rather than the exact match `recognized` reports",
  "observation": [["move", "Y", "by", "Z"], ["stop", "Y"]],
  "transform": {
    "base": "part_move",
    "dims": [1, 3],
    "deltas": [[["X", "Y"]], [["D", "Z"]]],
    "transforms": [
      {"dim": 1, "kind": "subst", "delta": [["X", "Y"]]},
      {"dim": 3, "kind": "subst", "delta": [["D", "Z"]]}
    ]
  }
}
```

**Fields that changed:** `note` (text now says "UNDER A TRANSFORM" instead of the plain
null wording) and the ADDED `transform` key. **Fields that did NOT change (the semantics
this fixture exists to protect):** `covered_by` ("part_move", same base shape) and
`minted` (`false`, still no growth) — the discriminative-null guarantee is intact; only the
recognition PATH is now more precise (transform vs exact) instead of collapsing both into
one undifferentiated "recognized".

`tests/test_composer_driver_migrated.py::test_dynamic_quantization_loop_mints_then_recognizes_on_regrowth`
(not a frozen-fixture test, but in the same file and gated by the same upgrade) needed a
similar, non-fixture reconciliation: its partially-covered observation used distinct filler
tokens (`P`/`Q`) on the relation it intended to already be "covered" by `part_move` — under
`wild_objects=true` that didn't matter, but literal decode requires an exact relation match,
so the test's observation/codebook-growth part were changed to reuse `part_move`'s own
literal fillers (`X`/`D`), isolating the test back down to its intended single novel relation
(`zzznew`). The mint-exactly-once / uncovered / discriminative-null semantics this whole
suite protects are UNCHANGED — see `tests/test_transform_decode_migrated.py`'s own
organic-pipeline test for the general (not fixture-specific) proof of the same discriminative
win (a genuinely INCONSISTENT substitution still mints, exactly once).


Part C0 of the migration design (see the design doc referenced in the task that produced
this directory). These fixtures capture the CURRENT (unmodified) Python behaviour of:

- `domains.reflective_faculty.compose_design_for_goal` (the beam composer)
- `domains.reflective_faculty.induce_concern` (coverage-then-mint)
- `domains.reflective_faculty.ground_concern` (the 7-way relation-head dispatch + PATH-2)
- `domains.question_driver.QuestionDriver.drive` (the driver reflex, 6 pack shapes)

They are the GROUND TRUTH the future graph-native reimplementations (the Rust `ShapeDecode`
Term, the seeded `composer_dispatch`/`shape_decode_loop` rules, the graph-resident
`question_driving` reflex) must reproduce. Generated by `capture.py` in this directory,
which can be re-run at any time:

```
cd gamma-substrate && PYTHONPATH=.:runners/dsl/python python3 \
  tests/fixtures/composer_driver_parity/capture.py
```

`capture.py` does not modify any source file. It DOES transiently exercise the live
`teach()` facility (see below) and restores the one seed file it perturbs before exiting.

## Files

- `composer.json` — 3 `compose_design_for_goal` cases over 3 hand-authored `ShapeSignature`
  parts (`part_move`, `part_detect`, `part_build`, each 2 relations): `full_cover` (goal =
  two parts' own relations, residual empty), `partial_cover` (goal = one part's relations +
  one relation no part expresses, residual non-empty), `beam_vs_greedy` (a 3-part, 6-relation
  goal run with `beam=1,cand_k=1` — the old-greedy discriminative control — and again with
  the default `beam=3,cand_k=3`, both captured for comparison).
- `induce_concern.json` — 2 cases over the same 3 parts: `covered` (an observation whose
  predicates+arity match `part_move`'s signature exactly, object fillers differ — the null,
  nothing minted) and `uncovered` (novel predicates `zwoop`/`florb`/`quix`, no held part
  matches — mints a `CapabilityAxis`; its full node attrs are dumped too).
- `ground_concern.json` — `relation_head_cases`: one case per relation head
  (comprehend/utility/group/control/communicate/decompose/construct/distribute), each a
  fresh `boot_core()` substrate + the `relation_vocabulary`/`syntactic_construction_cue`/
  `distributional_function_cue` seeds loaded (the real RelationCue lexicon, via
  `substrate.seed_loader.manifest_for` — not hand-copied text) + one `CapabilityAxis` minted
  with `residual_predicates` chosen to fire exactly that head's cue and no other (see
  "keyword collision" below). Records the full return dict, the installed rule name(s), and
  `rule_count_before/after/delta` (a substrate-level cross-check, per the design doc's "check
  via the substrate"). Also `path2_feedback` (residual predicates `["from the prior",
  "bounded"]` — no relation-head cue matches, falls through to the PATH-2
  `generate_from_residual` Fold-iterate composer) and `no_cue_wall` (a genuinely-novel
  predicate outside the whole lexicon — the honest `predicate_grounding` wall).
- `driver.json` — 6 `QuestionDriver.drive` packs: `world` (the elliptic-torsion compute pack,
  stubbed verify/answer_call, reused from `scripts/jabberwock_drives_itself.ELLIPTIC_PACK`),
  `know` ("What is HTTP?", a real local `wiki_local` read, no network), `meta` ("How do you
  want to retrieve information?" routed to `reflective_faculty.reflect` over
  `boot_reflective_substrate()`), `compound` ("What is HTTP and <elliptic question>", 2
  mixed-faculty subgoals), `contrast` ("compare HTTP with FTP", after
  `acquire_compare_construction` — the comparison construction must be acquired first, same
  as `scripts/jabberwock_crosses_comprehension_frontier.py`), and `gap_path` (an ungrounded
  question with `ask=None`, the default, so the comprehension stall falls into
  `parse_with_gaps` instead of the ASK loop — this question is pre-taught via
  `seeds/resolved_queries.json`, so the trace exercises BOTH the typed-gap parse AND a
  from-held-knowledge resolution, not merely a wall). Each `emission` is a small serialized
  dict (see `capture._serialize_emission`) with exactly the fields the design doc named:
  target kind/grounded/op, is_wall, wall_kind, missing, answer, verified, confidence,
  know_answer, meta_answer top-level keys + a shallow (bounded) summary of their values,
  subgoal count/kinds/is_wall, asks count, gap_frame presence + focus + typed-gap kinds, and
  note. `compound`/`contrast` also carry `subgoal_emissions` (one serialized Emission per
  child goal).

## Keyword collision found while designing the ground_concern cases

`ground_concern`'s PATH-1 grounds residual predicates by SUBSTRING match against the held
`RelationCue` keyword lexicon (`_residual_relations`). The bare predicate `"group"` does
**not** hit the `compose_whole_object` cue (the "order-N whole" grouping head) — it hits
`map_part_to_part`'s keyword list instead (`"group"` is one of that cue's keywords, in its
mathematical-group sense), which does not route `ground_concern`'s dispatch at all (relation
head `"map"` is not one of the 7 dispatched heads, so it would have looked like a "no
matching relation head" case, not a `group` case, if used naively). Verified empirically
(not by reading the JSON by eye) before picking `"co-moving"` instead, which is unique to
`compose_whole_object`'s keyword list. This is a note about CURRENT lexicon content, not a
bug fixed here — worth carrying into the migration (composer_dispatch / the seeded
lexicon should probably disambiguate `"group"` if the mathematical-group sense stays or an
explicit head-scoped cue is added).

## seeds/programs.json — transiently perturbed, restored

`ground_concern`'s PATH-2 (`generate_from_residual`) calls `teach_program`, which calls
`domains.teach.teach(agent, "Program", ..., category="programs")` — this **appends** a node
to `seeds/programs.json` (persisted host I/O, by design — see `domains/teach.py`). Because
`seeds/programs.json` was ALREADY modified in the working tree before this task began (an
unrelated prior session's output, not part of the committed baseline), `capture.py` does
**not** `git checkout` it (that would also discard that unrelated pre-existing change). It
instead snapshots the file's exact bytes before running section 3 and restores them
byte-for-byte afterward (`_ProgramsJsonGuard` in `capture.py`), regardless of whether the
working tree was clean or already dirty. Confirmed via `diff` against the snapshot after
every run in this task — no drift. The fixture only needs `ground_concern`'s **returned
dict**, not the seed file mutation, per the design doc.

No other seed files are touched: `categorise_by_shape` (teach's default category chooser)
reads `MetaShape` nodes, none of which exist on the minimal `boot_core()` substrates this
script builds, so it always falls through and the explicit `category="programs"` argument
is what actually decides the file (confirmed: `git status --short seeds/` showed only
`programs.json` touched, and only during PATH-2's capture).

## Determinism

Every case was run **twice in fresh interpreter processes** (`python3
tests/fixtures/composer_driver_parity/capture.py`, twice, diffing the four JSON outputs).

- `composer.json`, `induce_concern.json`, `ground_concern.json`: byte-identical across
  repeated fresh-process runs (rule_idx / node-id values are stable because `boot_core()`
  loads the same fixed `CORE_SEEDS` in the same order every time, so allocation order is
  deterministic).
- `driver.json`: ONE unstable field was found and is called out explicitly in the fixture
  itself (not silently frozen): in the `gap_path` case, the first gap-grounding subgoal
  ("What is would?") resolves via `wiki_local`'s title search for the bare word "would",
  and that search is **not deterministic** run-to-run — `present=True` with article
  "English modal auxiliary verbs" about half the time, an honest wall the other half
  (confirmed over 6+ standalone runs; ~50/50). This is a `wiki_local` search-layer
  nondeterminism (SQLite/parquet lookup for an ambiguous common word), not a
  driver/comprehension issue — every OTHER field in every case, including `gap_path`'s
  top-level `is_wall`/`note`/`answer`/`gap_frame_focus`/`gap_kinds` and its OTHER 3
  subgoals, was byte-identical across every run. `driver.json`'s `gap_path.emission`
  therefore has `subgoal_is_wall: null` (masked, not the flaky value) plus a
  `_unstable_fields_excluded` note recording exactly what was excluded and why. Wall-clock
  `elapsed_s` timings were also measured during authoring (to size the script — `know` /
  `compound` / `contrast` / `gap_path` hit the real local `wiki_local` parquet store, ~1-30s
  each; `world` / `meta` are sub-second) but are printed to stdout only, never written into
  the fixture (the design doc's "note the unstable fields and exclude them").

Part D's parity tests should not assert on `driver.json["gap_path"]["emission"]
["subgoal_is_wall"]` (or any timing) — everything else in these four files is safe to assert
byte-for-byte / value-for-value.

## Things that were surprising while capturing current behaviour

- `ground_concern`'s dispatch order genuinely matters: `"decompose"` and `"communicate"`
  BOTH route to `_compose_communicate_rule` (confirmed in `relation_head_cases.decompose`,
  whose installed rule is still named `communicate_what_i_see_...` but with the
  `decompose`-only effects — no `action: produce_utterance` attr on the minted subgoal,
  since that requires `"communicate"` too) — this matches the design doc's B2 note that
  "communicate and decompose both → composer 'communicate'" exactly.
- `compose_design_for_goal`'s "Covers" check compares whole relation TUPLES between the goal
  and a held part's OWN signature relations, wildcarding only the part's own non-predicate
  slots — it is not unifying the goal's role-fillers against the part's variables. A goal
  relation like `["move", "A", "by", "B"]` is NOT covered by `part_move`'s
  `["move", "X", "by", "D"]` (different literal fillers on the GOAL side, and Covers'
  wildcarding runs the other direction); only a goal relation that is one of the part's own
  literal relations (or literally shares the part's canonical filler tokens, e.g. `"PRIOR"`,
  `"SELF"`, `"UNIT"`, as the codebase's real ShapeSignatures do throughout `seeds/
  relation_vocabulary.json`-adjacent data) gets covered. The first draft of these fixtures
  used distinct per-goal filler tokens (`"A"`, `"B"`) and silently produced a WRONG "partial
  cover" result for what was meant to be a full-cover case — caught by checking
  `covered_count`/`ordered_parts` against hand expectations before trusting the capture, not
  by reading the composer's docstring alone.
- `boot_reflective_substrate()`'s `installed` report includes two `FAILED` entries
  (`domains.lvp_subseeds`, `domains.communication_concepts` — both modules do not exist in
  the current working tree; this mirrors the wider pre-existing deletion of many
  `domains/*.py` files visible in `git status` at the start of this task) — the `meta` case's
  `held_concepts` therefore reads as an empty dict (0 concepts), not the ~8+ concepts the
  `epistemic_access` faculty would normally hold. This is captured faithfully (current
  behaviour is current behaviour) rather than worked around; a future fixture refresh after
  those modules are restored/removed-for-good will look different, which is expected and
  fine — the migrated graph-native driver only needs to match ground_concern/compose/
  induce_concern/drive's OWN logic, not paper over an unrelated missing-module regression.
